21_cold_dopamine:
One hour at 14°C.
Noradrenaline +530%, dopamine +250% (Sramek et al., 2000). But that was an hour, not a 3-minute dip.
We dose it: temperature, time, timing.
How long do you stay in?
#sumisura #coldplunge #dopamine #icebath #brussels
22_cold_14_vs_20:
20°C or 14°C? It changes everything.
Metabolism +93% at 20°C vs +350% at 14°C, and the noradrenaline surge only showed up at 14°C (Sramek et al., 2000).
Temperature is the dose.
How cold is your plunge?
#sumisura #coldplunge #icebath #coldexposure #brussels
23_cold_sauna_winter_swimmers:
Cold + sauna: what it does over time.
Winter swimmers who alternate cold dips and sauna burned more energy when cooled than controls (Soberg et al., 2021). Small study, 8 men.
Cold first or heat first?
#sumisura #contrasttherapy #coldplunge #sauna #brussels
24_sauna_dry_vs_humid:
Dry or humid sauna? Your heart can tell.
Heart rate +60% (80°C dry), +90% (100°C dry), +130% (80°C humid); noradrenaline +100/+160/+310% (Kukkonen-Harjula et al., 1989).
Humidity raises the load.
Dry or humid?
#sumisura #sauna #heat #hearthealth #brussels
25_sauna_brain:
Sauna and your brain.
4–7 sessions a week were associated with about 66% lower dementia risk vs once a week, over 20 years (Laukkanen et al., 2017). Association, not proof.
How often do you sauna?
#sumisura #sauna #brainhealth #longevity #brussels
26_sauna_stress_hormones:
A week of sauna: what happened to cortisol?
After 7 days of 1 h at 80°C twice a day, cortisol and ACTH had slightly decreased (Leppäluoto et al., 1986).
Heat is a stressor. Dosed right, the body adapts.
Does sauna calm you down?
#sumisura #sauna #cortisol #stress #brussels
27_sauna_after_training_hr:
Sauna after training: your resting heart rate.
Well-trained cyclists added 30 min of sauna after training; heart rate on waking dropped about 10% (Stanley, Buchheit et al., 2015).
Heat after training, not instead of it.
Do you track your resting HR?
#sumisura #sauna #recovery #heartrate #brussels
28_heat_alone_strength:
Heat alone made muscles stronger.
10 weeks of heat on the thigh, no training: max isometric force +5.8% (Goto et al., 2011).
An extra stimulus, not a replacement.
Would you have guessed?
#sumisura #heattraining #strength #sauna #brussels
29_heat_chamber_haemoglobin:
Easy riding in 38°C heat.
Elite cyclists rode one easy hour in a heat chamber, 5x a week for 5 weeks: haemoglobin mass increased vs training at normal temperature (Rønnestad et al., 2021).
Heat + movement: the idea behind Sauna Cycling.
Would you ride in 38°C?
#sumisura #saunacycling #heattraining #cycling #brussels
30_ihht_session:
40 minutes, lying down: an IHHT session.
Low-oxygen air through a mask, then oxygen-rich air, repeated, with your oxygen saturation tracked the whole time.
No sweat. Still a stimulus.
Had you heard of IHHT?
#sumisura #ihht #hypoxia #oxygen #brussels
31_ihht_screening:
IHHT isn't for everyone.
Pregnancy, anaemia or a heart condition need a closer look first, so every member fills in a health questionnaire before starting.
Safety first. Then the stimulus.
#sumisura #ihht #safety #health #brussels
32_redlight_morning:
3 minutes. Morning only.
3 min of 670 nm light in the morning improved colour contrast vision by 17% on average; in the afternoon, no effect (Shinhmar et al., 2021).
Timing is part of the dose.
Did you know timing mattered?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #mitochondria #science #brussels
33_redlight_sore_muscles:
Sore after training? Red light data.
A meta-analysis of 14 trials found less soreness and a large effect on strength at 24–48 h (Tsou et al., 2025).
A recovery tool, not a training plan.
Have you tried it?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #recovery #doms #brussels
34_redlight_distance_dose:
Same panel. Different dose.
Closer to the panel, more light reaches your skin; further away, less. Distance and time set your dose.
So we set both, every session.
How close do you sit?
#sumisura #redlighttherapy #photobiomodulation #recovery #brussels
35_breathing_6_per_minute:
6 breaths a minute.
Around 6 breaths per minute, heart and breathing resonate and heart rate variability peaks (Lehrer & Gevirtz, 2014).
Shiftwave guides you there. We measure it.
Can you breathe this slowly?
#sumisura #breathwork #hrv #shiftwave #brussels
36_hrv_breathing_measurement:
Your HRV score can lie.
Breathe slower and your HRV reading goes up in the moment. That's measurement, not adaptation (Eckberg, 2009).
So we measure the same way, every time.
Do you track HRV?
#sumisura #hrv #whoop #nervoussystem #brussels
37_shiftwave_biodrive:
A chair that follows your pulse.
Shiftwave sends pulsed pressure waves along your body; in some protocols BioDrive adapts them to your pulse, live.
Designed to shift your nervous system. We track the result.
Would you try it?
#sumisura #shiftwave #nervoussystem #recovery #brussels
38_vo2max_fitness_strength:
Fitness or strength? You need both.
In 70,913 adults, the fittest had 35% lower mortality and the strongest grip 21% lower, each independent of the other (Kim et al., 2018).
Which one do you train more?
#sumisura #vo2max #strength #longevity #brussels
39_vo2max_no_ceiling:
Fitness has no ceiling.
In 122,007 treadmill-tested patients, the elite group had the lowest risk of all, with no upper limit of benefit (Mandsager et al., 2018). An association.
Do you know your VO2max?
#sumisura #vo2max #longevity #fitness #brussels
40_metabolic_flexibility:
Pro cyclist vs metabolic syndrome.
Pros burned more fat and produced less lactate during exercise; the two moved in opposite directions (San-Millán & Brooks, 2018).
That's metabolic flexibility, and what our Metabolic Scan measures.
Do you know your fat-burning zone?
#sumisura #metabolichealth #zone2 #vo2max #brussels
